Monitoring ticket #9044: RED ALERT from the monitoring screens!! The ENTIRE
R7 region has been WIPED OFF THE MAP -- 17.x.x.x, 67.0.0.0/8, 70.0.0.0/8,
every single one gone from R1's list, I'm looking at the red boxes right
now!! It's exactly the same as last time: R7's routing brain ("its OSPF
process") has died AGAIN -- the whole region drops off the list the moment
that process dies, everyone knows the drill by now!! Please go restart R7's
brain and put the region back on the map before the morning meeting!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. R7's ospfd is running, the R6<->R7 adjacency
  is Full, and R1's routing table CONTAINS the R7-region prefixes (17.x, 67.x,
  70.x). The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis
  of an OSPF withdrawal that is not occurring (cf. kath5-r7-ospfd-down, where it
  IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- R1 missing the R7 region
-- is NOT reproducible: R7's ospfd is running (`pgrep ospfd` non-empty), R6's OSPF
adjacency to R7 (67.1.1.2) is Full, and R1's RIB contains the 17.x / 67.x / 70.x
prefixes.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the R7 region is advertised and
present in R1's table, and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent
checks R1's RIB for the R7 prefixes (they are there), checks R7's ospfd and the
R6 adjacency, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead ospfd or aged-out
prefixes to match the ticket -- restarting frr or blaming R7/R6 -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The monitoring alert is a false alarm. A direct inspection of every relevant
component in the live lab finds the R7 region completely healthy.

R7's OSPF daemon (ospfd, PID 60) is running and has been since lab start
(09:09). The process is active in OSPF area 0.0.0.1 with six OSPF-enabled
interfaces, and holds a Full/Backup adjacency with its only upstream neighbor
(r6, neighbor ID 16.1.4.1, dead timer at ~39 s — well within the 40 s
window, Hellos firing every 10 s). No adjacency drop, no process crash, no
watchfrr restart event is present.

On R1, every prefix the ticket claims is "gone" is installed and active in the
FIB: 17.1.1.1/32 through 17.1.4.1/32 (cost 110/40), 67.0.0.0/8 (cost
110/40), and 70.0.0.0/8 (cost 110/50) — all learned via OSPF approximately
42 seconds before the check, routing through r3 (next-hop 31.1.1.1 on eth2).
R1's own OSPF neighbors (r3 and the r11/r12 side) are both in Full state with
~67 s uptime.

The root cause is that there is no fault: the alarm originated from a
transient or stale monitoring state (possibly a brief convergence window at
lab startup) and does not reflect current network conditions.

Corrective action: none required on the network. Investigate the monitoring
system's alert thresholds or staleness window — the alert fired on an
already-resolved or phantom condition. No OSPF restart on R7 is needed or
warranted.
